notes: 66 of the 97 'Global perspectives' units are not social science: 63 are Visual Arts units (unit.115-126, 137-147, 268-282, 291-302, 420-437; 420-437 also carry a find-and-replace garbling 'Visual arts' over 'Art'), unit.156 and unit.286 each merge two units into one record, unit.438 is 'Natural Resources' (G4) with 'Earth' garbled; all left unmapped with the reason in 'why'.

The school teaches geography and history in G1-G2 (states of India, continents, early humans, farming, trade) a stage ahead of NCF, whose foundational rows carry neither subject; those units are pinned to cognitive and socio-emotional rows (F.C-7.1, C-2.2, C-8.8, C-4.1, C-9.5) and the fit is weak. A better crosswalk needs either the preparatory World Around Us rows applied to G1-G2 or a school-defined target.

NCF's preparatory stage has no history or civics strand: World Around Us has no row for heroes, leaders, national symbols or inventions. The school's units on these are pinned to the nearest rows, C-2.3 (change over time as told by elders and local stories), C-2.1 (human-made systems) and C-4.7 (values and dispositions).

NCERT's 2019 secondary outcomes are five process bundles per class built on the CBSE syllabus. They give no evidence for NCF S.C-1.4 (indigenous knowledge systems, left empty) and only thin evidence for S.C-1.2, S.C-8.3 and S.C-9.1 (ancient India's chronology, economy and contributions). Grade 9 'Individuals in Society' has no NCERT outcomes of its own; its rows are evidenced by the class-9 process outcomes 9.02-9.05 only.

NCERT class-6 outcomes 6.01-6.03 (stars, planets, satellites; zones of the earth; day, night and seasons) sit on the science boundary and are mapped to M.C-6.1 (natural phenomena) as the nearest social-science row; the science seat may also claim them. 6.08 (superstitions about eclipses) is read as M.C-2.2, the continued prevalence of beliefs, examined against M.C-6.1.
